coordinates.locator: Meyrin Site – Point 1 (CERN and its Neighbours)
coordinates.note: REVIEW REQUIRED (A17), after real effort: no CERN geodetic-survey or metrology publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the underground ATLAS cavern was found (searched CERN survey/metrology conference papers, the ATLAS JINST detector paper, CERN's neighbours/open-days pages for Point 1, and Wikipedia's own infobox, which itself carries no citation for its coordinate). The numeric value is inherited from an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim centroid for the surface enclosure named 'CERN - Point 1 (ATLAS)' (kept as src:cern-point-1-osm-nominatim in the record's top-level sources for provenance); that geocoder source is not cited on this coordinate because A17 forbids a geocoder backing a `detector`-kind point. precision_m widened from 300 to 500 m to reflect that this is an unsurveyed estimate.

depth.note: Rock overburden above the ATLAS cavern; home.cern states the same figure ('It sits in a cavern 100 m below ground near the main CERN site').
depth.quote: ATLAS has the dimensions of a cylinder, 46m long, 25m in diameter, and sits in a cavern 100m below ground.

depth_rock.quote: sits in a cavern 100m below ground

name: LHC Point 1 (ATLAS cavern)
notes: REVIEW REQUIRED (A17): no official CERN or geodetic publication giving WGS84 coordinates for LHC Point 1 was found after real effort (cds.cern.ch is behind bot protection; home.cern and atlas.cern state only that ATLAS 'sits in a cavern 100 m below ground near the main CERN site, close to the village of Meyrin'). The coordinate value is a geocoder estimate; see coordinates.note.

summary.plain: The underground cavern at the edge of CERN's Meyrin campus where the ATLAS detector sits, about 100 metres below ground. It is one of the eight access points around the 27-kilometre Large Hadron Collider ring and the place where two of the LHC's proton beams are made to collide inside ATLAS.
summary.technical: LHC interaction point 1 on the CERN Meyrin site: the UX15 experimental cavern ~100 m below the surface housing the ATLAS detector, together with its surface buildings and the ATLAS control room.
